continuity_scope: Netflix/Riot animated Arcane continuity, restricted to the opening Season 1 material in Netflix Tudum's official Season 1 recap section “Who are Vi and Powder?”: introduction of the young sisters from Zaun, Vander taking them in, their childhood-friend group, an early Piltover heist, and the blue-crystal explosion. Netflix's official series page is used only to establish the animated-series identity and twin-cities premise. League of Legends game canon, promotional alternate universes, later Arcane episodes/seasons, and all other Riot media are excluded.

Netflix Tudum, “ARCANE Season One Ending Recap,” opening section “Who are Vi and Powder?”
coverage_rule: Include every named individual dramatic figure in the selected official opening-recap section: Vi, Powder, Vander, Mylo, and Claggor. Piltover, Zaun, twin-city social structure, childhood, heist, magical crystals, the inventor's home, the explosion, technology, magic, factions, policing, places, and class conflict are terms/context rather than nodes. Jinx, Silco, Jayce, and every later named figure are omitted even where the official recap later discusses them; no later name/identity is applied to Powder.
omissions: All people first named only outside the selected opening-recap section, including Jinx, Silco, Jayce, and every other later Season 1/Season 2 individual.

All later events and characterization, including future names/identities, deaths, arrests, mental-health framing, disability, policing/enforcer conduct, family separation, gang/faction membership, combat abilities, and magical/technological developments.

League of Legends game canon, promotional alternate universes, other Riot media, official merchandise as story evidence, fan wikis, Wikipedia, databases, reviews, non-official recaps, social posts, and unlicensed transcripts.

Ethnicity/cultural coding, exact ages, adoption/legal custody, biological family history, a general class analysis, and moral claims about magic/technology, none of which are substantiated in this bounded official text.
uncertainties: The selected Netflix recap calls Vi and Powder young girls, kids, sisters from Zaun, and says Vander takes them in to raise as his own. It does not state numerical ages, legal adoption, custody status, biology beyond sisterhood, or a later family outcome.

The official opening section says the group enters Piltover on a heist, Powder finds magical blue crystals, and an explosion occurs. It does not establish a complete technology/magic system, individual culpability, injuries/deaths, law-enforcement response, or moral evaluation.

Netflix's series logline calls Piltover and Zaun twin cities in discord. Its later official recap contains social/class and later-plot explanations, but this source pass does not turn city origin into ethnicity/cultural coding or import later political claims.

The animated series is based on a video game according to Netflix metadata, but the evidence here is specific to Arcane's animation continuity and never assumes game-character identities, abilities, or chronology.
evidence_basis: Official Netflix and Netflix Tudum materials only. Tudum's selected opening recap passage provides named character/action claims; the Netflix title page establishes the animated-series/twin-cities framing. The later portions of the same recap are expressly excluded.
